newsitem.title: USA: UTILICORP ON TARGET FOR EARNINGS GOALS.
newsitem.headline: UTILICORP ON TARGET FOR EARNINGS GOALS.

text.p: UtiliCorp United Inc Thursday reported a 27 percent increase in second quarter earnings per share saying it remains committed to achieving an average of eight percent growth in earnings per share over the next several years, beginning this year.
"So far this year we are very much on target," noted Chief Executive Officer Richard Green Jr.
The company earned $0.38 per share in the latest quarter compared to $0.30 a year earlier on a normalized basis, eliminating the non-recurring item booked in last year's second quarter.
Normalized six-month earnings were $1.22 per share versus $1.09 in the first six months of 1996, and normalized 12-month earnings were $2.24 per share versus $2.21 a year earlier.

Green said the 27 percent growth in second quarter earnings per share reflects continued strong growth at Aquila Energy Marketing, increased earnings from independent power projects, and a three percent decrease in operating expenses.
Interest expense decreased six percent due to early retirement of high-coupon notes in the 1997 first quarter.
UtiliCorp said earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) declined in the 1997 quarter.
EBIT slipped to $67.2 million from $80.9 million.
It said Aquila Energy's EBIT from wholesale businesses rose about $3 million compared to a year earlier.
Aquila's second quarter EBIT from retail gas marketing declined $4 million from last year's level.
The company said it expects performance of these operations to improve as they continue to benefit from Aquila's broad gas marketing expertise and infrastructure.
It said Aquila's gas pipeline operations had slightly lower EBIT than a year ago due to a decline in the price of natural gas and natural gas liquids.
The company said it expects pipeline throughput to decline during the second half of the year because of recent well connection activity that is lower than expected.

UtiliCorp's Energy Delivery segment, consisting of domestic electric and gas distribution utilities in eight states, had EBIT that was the same as in the 1996 quarter in spite of cooler than normal weather this June. Results reflect new gas rates in Michigan, Nebraska and Kansas, a 2 percent increase in the number of electric and gas distribution customers, and savings from a renegotiated purchased power contract in Colorado.

Earnings before interest and taxes from international operations were down about $4.8 million in the second quarter compared to a year earlier, due mainly to timing of Australian and New Zealand earnings.
